primary_sources: Photograph of Attlee, Truman, and Stalin at Potsdam, summer 1945

stimulus.text: Color photograph of the three Allied leaders seated in wicker chairs outdoors at the Potsdam Conference, Germany, in late July or early August 1945. From left to right: British Prime Minister Clement Attlee, in a dark suit; President Harry S. Truman, in a dark suit and bow tie, holding papers; and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin, in a white military tunic. Four advisers stand behind them: Admiral William Leahy, Foreign Minister Ernest Bevin, Secretary of State James Byrnes, and Foreign Minister Vyacheslav Molotov.
stimulus.source_note: Photograph by a U.S. Army Signal Corps photographer, Potsdam, circa July 28 to August 1, 1945 (USA C-1860, U.S. National Archives). Public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government. Viewed before use. Attlee replaced Churchill as British prime minister during the conference, after the British election of July 1945.

source: original; stimulus drawn from book-grounded paraphrases, tables, and photographs (see source_note)
stem: Two of the three seated leaders differ from the men in the Yalta photograph. What changed between February and July 1945?

options.text: Stalin had died and been replaced by Foreign Minister Molotov
options.misconception: Stalin stayed in power and sat at Potsdam; Molotov stood behind him.

options.text: Churchill had resigned and been replaced by Anthony Eden
options.misconception: Churchill led the British delegation at first, and Attlee, not Eden, replaced him.

options.text: Roosevelt had died and Churchill had lost the British election
Truman had resigned and been replaced by Secretary Byrnes
options.misconception: Truman stayed president through the conference; Byrnes served as his secretary of state.

rationales.A: Background from the books: Stalin stayed in power and sat at Potsdam; Molotov stood behind him.
rationales.B: Background from the books: Churchill led the British delegation at first, and Attlee, not Eden, replaced him.
rationales.C: Roosevelt died in April 1945, so Truman took his seat, and Churchill lost the British election in July, so Attlee replaced him during the conference.
rationales.D: Background from the books: Truman stayed president through the conference; Byrnes served as his secretary of state.
rationales.general:
1. The photograph shows Attlee, Truman, and Stalin seated together at Potsdam.
2. At Yalta the seats had held Churchill, Roosevelt, and Stalin.
3. Background: Roosevelt died in April 1945, and Churchill lost the British election held during the conference.
4. Attlee took Churchill's seat partway through, so two of the three faces changed in five months.
Remember: a photograph's date matters, because leaders can change fast in wartime.
